newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Anti-euthanasia bill tabled in parliament.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Anti-euthanasia bill tabled in parliament.

text.p: Conservative Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Monday backed a plan for his national government to over-ride the world's first voluntary euthanasia law, which took effect in the Northern Territory in July.
Government backbencher Kevin Andrews introduced a private bill in parliament's lower house on Monday aimed at overturning the law, which allows doctors to help terminally ill patients commit suicide.
"It is one of those issues which is in essence a life and death matter," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"It is a matter of principle, it goes to the essence of what we see life to be and the sanctity of it and the importance of it and the quality of it," Howard said.
Despite his opposition to the assisted suicide law, Howard will allow a conscience vote on the bill and not demand his colleagues toe a party line.
"I've stated my position on euthanasia in the past. I don't intend to force that view down the throats of any of my colleagues," Howard said.
"This is a very difficult, sensitive issue and there are passionately held views on both sides," he said.
The anti-euthanasia bill is expected to be voted on during the current parliamentary session which ends in December.
Australia's national government has the power to over-ride laws in the country's two territories, but not the six states.
While the euthanasia law took effect from July, it has not yet been used, with doctors unsure of their legal position in the face of court and parliamentary challenges to the law.

Separate efforts to strike out the law through the territory's parliament and supreme court failed earlier this year and the law still faces a constitutional challenge in the country's peak court, the High Court.
The voluntary euthanasia law has sparked strong condemnation from political, church, Aboriginal and community leaders, but opinion polls show strong public support.
Euthanasia is illegal in Australia's other territory and six states, but doctors say it is unofficially practised.
